data.long_meaning: Madesh is a Sanskrit name derived from the word 'Mada', which means 'measure'. The name is associated with Lord Shiva, who is often referred to as the 'Lord of Measures'. It signifies precision, accuracy, and balance. The name Madesh carries the meaning “God of Measures” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Madesh usually hope their child will grow to embody god of measures and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the divine balance in life.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Madesh total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

data.spiritual_significance: In Hinduism, Madesh is believed to be a divine name, associated with Lord Shiva, the destroyer of evil and the god of creation, preservation, and transformation. By giving the name Madesh to a child, parents are imparting a spiritual connection to Lord Shiva, his qualities, and his blessings. The name is considered auspicious and sacred in Hindu tradition.

historical_references.reference: Madesh was a famous Jain Tirthankara, the 23rd in the present cycle of 24 Tirthankaras. He is believed to have lived during the 10th Century BCE in the Magadha region of ancient India.

Madesh or Mahadeva, also known as Shiva, is regarded as the god of the Hindu triumvirate or Trimurti, representing the creator aspect. He is believed to have originated in the Indian subcontinent in the pre-Vedic period, around 5000 BCE.
